problems.title: Sum two cotangents using a product-to-sum formula
problems.question: Find cot(15°-β)+cot(15°+β) if 0<β<π/2 and cos2β=5/13.
problems.idea: Combine the cotangents into one fraction.
steps: Here U+V=30° and U-V=-2β.
Thus the numerator is 1/2 and the denominator is [5/13-√3/2]/2.
The denominator is nonzero, as required.

problems.title: Prove a tangent identity on its full domain
problems.question: Prove tan3α-tan2α-tanα=tan3α·tan2α·tanα.
problems.idea: Apply the tangent addition identity to 3α=2α+α.
formulas: tan(U+V)=(tanU+tanV)/(1-tanUtanV), when all terms are defined.
steps: Write tan3α(1-tan2αtanα)=tan2α+tanα.
Expand and move tan2α,tanα to the left.
This gives exactly the requested identity.
All of tanα,tan2α,tan3α must exist, so require cosα·cos2α·cos3α≠0.
problems.answer: The identity holds wherever all its tangent terms are defined.
problems.note: The printed restriction α≠πk/2 is insufficient: for example, α=π/4 still makes tan2α undefined.

problems.title: Distance from a parallel line to a plane
problems.question: Parallel lines a,b lie in plane δ, 4 cm apart. A third line c is parallel to them and is 5 cm from a and 6 cm from b. Find its distance to δ.
problems.idea: Cut all three parallel lines by a perpendicular plane.
formulas: Distance equations in the cross-section are x²+h²=25 and (x-4)²+h²=36.
steps: In the perpendicular cross-section, a,b become points (0,0),(4,0), while c becomes (x,h).
Subtract: 16-8x=36-25=11, giving x=5/8.
The nonnegative distance is h=15√7/8.

problems.title: Range of a mixed sine and cosine expression
problems.question: Find the range of y=cos²x+sinx.
problems.idea: Set t=sinx and replace cos²x by 1-t².
steps: The maximum is 5/4, attained when t=1/2.
At the endpoints t=-1 and t=1 the values are -1 and 1; the minimum is -1.
Continuity gives every value between these bounds.

problems.title: Construct one of many cosine-product representations
problems.question: Find at least one triple x,y,z such that (1+cos199+cos398)/2=cosx cosy cosz. Angles without a degree mark are in radians.
problems.idea: Two angles can be zero, leaving a single cosine to match the target.
steps: Let L=(1+cos199+cos398)/2. The double-angle identity also gives L=cos199(cos199+1/2).
Numerically cos199≈-0.471626 and L≈-0.013382, so L is in [-1,1].
Choose y=z=0 and x=arccosL≈1.584179 radians.
Then cosx cosy cosz=L·1·1=L exactly; the arccos expression specifies the exact value.
problems.note: The question asks for one triple and imposes no integer or special-angle restriction. Infinitely many triples are possible.

problems.title: Angle between an inclined line and a line in the plane
problems.question: A segment makes 45° with a plane. A line through its foot in the plane makes 45° with the segment’s projection. Find the acute angle between the line and segment.
problems.idea: Only the horizontal projection contributes to their dot product.
steps: Both given angles are 45°.
The acute angle is θ=60°.

problems.title: Distinct triangle angles allow cancellation
problems.question: Triangle angles A≠B satisfy sin(A-B)=sin²A-sin²B. Classify the triangle.
problems.idea: Factor the squared-sine difference with a sum-to-product identity.
steps: Because A,B are distinct triangle angles, -π<A-B<π and A-B≠0, so sin(A-B)≠0.
Cancel it to get sin(A+B)=1.
Since 0<A+B<π, this means A+B=π/2.
The remaining angle C=π-(A+B)=π/2.
problems.note: The original source uses sin²A-sin²B. Reading those superscripts as sin2A-sin2B would give a different, incorrect conclusion for this question.

problems.title: Construct every box section through three edge points
problems.question: In rectangular box ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, M∈A₁B₁, N∈B₁C₁ and K∈CD. Construct the plane section through M,N,K, including all cases.
problems.idea: Find the plane’s intersections with the twelve edges; join consecutive intersections lying on a common face.
formulas: Use normalized box coordinates A=(0,0,0),B=(1,0,0),D=(0,1,0),A₁=(0,0,1). Write M=(m,0,1),N=(1,n,1),K=(k,1,0).
Put $c=1-m+n(m-k)$ and $d=nk-(1-m)$. The plane equation is $nx-(1-m)y-cz=d$.
For an edge U+t(V-U), solve the plane equation for t; keep the intersection iff 0≤t≤1. An edge with both endpoints in the plane is included completely.
steps: Draw MN on the top face. The bottom-face trace through K is parallel to MN; extend it to the next bottom edge. Use the side faces to connect the resulting traces.
For interior edge points 0<m,n,k<1, set H=1-m-nk. If H>0, the plane also cuts AD,AA₁,CC₁, producing hexagon M-N-Q-K-L-P, where Q∈CC₁,L∈AD,P∈AA₁.
If H<0, the extra bottom intersection L lies on AB, and the section is pentagon M-N-Q-K-L. If H=0, L and P merge at A, giving pentagon M-N-Q-K-A.

If a supplied point is an edge endpoint, apply the same edge-intersection rule, merge duplicate vertices, and keep full coplanar edges. Boundary sections can be triangles, quadrilaterals or pentagons; generic six-vertex sections remain possible. If the three supplied points coincide or are collinear, they do not determine a unique plane.
problems.answer: For interior points: a hexagon when H>0, a pentagon when H≤0; use the edge rule for all endpoint and degenerate cases.

problems.title: Prove the sum-of-sines formula by telescoping
problems.question: Prove $\sum_{k=1}^n\sin(k\alpha)=\sin(n\alpha/2)\sin((n+1)\alpha/2)/\sin(\alpha/2)$.
problems.idea: Multiply by 2sin(α/2), turning each term into a difference of cosines.
steps: For each k, 2sin(α/2)sin(kα)=cos((k-1/2)α)-cos((k+1/2)α).
When summed, consecutive cosine terms cancel, leaving cos(α/2)-cos((n+1/2)α).
Use cosU-cosV=2sin((U+V)/2)sin((V-U)/2) to turn this into 2sin((n+1)α/2)sin(nα/2).
Divide by 2sin(α/2), nonzero under the stated restriction.
problems.note: The exact denominator restriction is α≠2πk. The source’s α≠πk is stronger than necessary but still makes the proof valid.

problems.title: Smallest right-triangle area from a distance to a tilted plane
problems.question: A plane γ passes through the hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC. Its angle with the triangle plane has cosα=1/4. C is distance m from γ. Find the least triangle area.
problems.idea: First recover the altitude to AB, then bound the hypotenuse.
formulas: m=h sinα; sinα=√15/4; for a right triangle h≤c/2; area=ch/2.
steps: The altitude from C to AB is h=m/(√15/4)=4m/√15.
In a right triangle, h=ab/c≤c/2 because 2ab≤a²+b²=c². Thus c≥2h.
The area is ch/2≥h².
Equality occurs in an isosceles right triangle, giving minimum h²=16m²/15.
problems.answer: 16m²/15, attained for an isosceles right triangle.
